# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Harper Grant**
Member ID: W271226534
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-19**
- Member: Harper Grant
- Member ID: W271226534
- Reference number: POC-06FC809FB2-91216
- Denied service: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
- Plan: Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Connecticut
- Governing policy: **Aetna CPB 0736 – Hip Preservation Surgery** (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0736.html)

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing Aetna's denial of the prior authorization request for my hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), issued on 2026-08-19 under reference number POC-06FC809FB2-91216. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. My surgeon, Duval, MD (orthopedic surgery), submitted this request with documentation that the procedure is needed, and I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision.

I am writing because the records already in my file appear to address the criteria that Aetna itself publishes in the policy named above. Below, I quote the plan's own language and point to the specific record that corresponds to each requirement. Where the records do not contain a detail, I say so plainly and ask that it be requested rather than treated as missing.

---

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

**1. Imaging diagnosis of definite FAI with labral pathology**

The policy states:

> "Diagnosis of definite femoro-acetabular impingement (FAI) defined by appropriate imaging studies (X-rays, MRI or CT scans), showing labral pathology (e.g. partial or full thickness labral tearing or labral damage) with one or more of the following:"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip dated 2026-07-17 reports an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement. That is both the required imaging study and the required labral pathology.

The policy's first listed form of impingement is:

> "cam impingement (alpha angle greater than 50 degrees)"

The same 2026-07-17 MRI arthrogram reports an **alpha angle of 68 degrees**. Only one of the listed findings is required, and this one is met by a clear margin.

The policy also states:

> "For purposes of this policy, Aetna will consider the official written report of complex imaging studies (e.g., CT, MRI, myelogram). If the operating surgeon disagrees with the official written report, the surgeon should document that disagreement."

The findings above come from the official written report of my MRI arthrogram. If that report is not in the file Aetna reviewed, I ask that it be obtained from Dr. Duval's office and read as part of this appeal.

**2. Moderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI, lasting at least 6 months**

The policy states:

> "Moderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI (hip or groin pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities, with duration of at least 6 months where diagnosis of FAI has been made as above; and"

My records document **12 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest** — twice the duration the policy asks for. They also document sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and that I cannot run or squat. That is pain in the location the policy names, brought on by the activities the policy names, limiting what I can do.

**3. Positive impingement sign**

The policy states:

> "Positive impingement sign with sudden pain on 90 degree hip flexion with adduction and internal rotation or extension and external rotation; and"

My examination records document **positive provocative testing on the affected side**, with range of motion limited by pain. The records as I have them do not spell out the exact degrees and directions of the maneuver used. Rather than have this treated as an absence, I ask Aetna to request the full office examination note from Dr. Duval, who performed the testing.

**4. Failure of conservative treatment, including the required course of physiotherapy**

The policy states:

> "Failure to respond to all available conservative treatment options including: activity modification (e.g., restriction of athletic pursuits and avoidance of symptomatic motion), pharmacological intervention (e.g., non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDS]), injections of local anesthetics into the joint) and physiotherapy."

Each of these is in my record:

- **Activity modification** — documented as part of my physical therapy program.
- **Medication** — NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection** — a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-10, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Physiotherapy** — supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization.

The policy then sets the amount of treatment required:

> "The treatment should be for at least 12 weeks in the past year with at least 6 weeks being formal physiotherapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist not virtual)."

My physical therapy ran **14 weeks, from 2026-04-18 to 2026-07-25, with 16 visits completed** — supervised, in-person therapy. That exceeds both the 12-week treatment requirement and the 6-week formal physiotherapy requirement stated in the policy, and it falls entirely within the past year.

On how that therapy is to be verified, the policy states:

> "Physical therapy (PT) needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history; and"

My therapy is documented in the **physical therapy discharge note**, which is one of the two forms of confirmation the policy accepts. My claims history for those 16 visits is a second, and it is already in Aetna's own possession. If the discharge note did not reach the reviewer, I ask that it be requested before a decision is made.

**5. Absence of advanced arthritis or joint space narrowing**

The policy states:

> "Absence of advanced osteoarthritis change on pre-operative X-ray (Tonnis grade 2 or more) or severe cartilage injury (Outerbridge grade III or IV); and"

and

> "Absence of joint space narrowing on plain radiograph of the pelvis. Joint space is not less than 2 mm wide anywhere along the sourcil; and"

My 2026-07-17 imaging reports **Tonnis grade 0** and **joint space preserved**. Tonnis grade 0 is well below the grade 2 threshold the policy sets. My records as provided do not state an Outerbridge cartilage grade or a millimeter measurement along the sourcil; if Aetna needs those specific values, I ask that my radiographs and reports be requested from Dr. Duval's office and from the imaging facility.

**6. Exclusionary conditions**

The policy states:

> "Member does not have generalized joint laxity especially in diseases connected with hypermobility of the joints, such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome; and"

and

> "Member does not have osteogenesis imperfecta; and"

I have no such diagnosis in my history. [To be confirmed in writing by Dr. Duval: absence of generalized joint laxity, Marfan syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and osteogenesis imperfacta.]

**7. Other sources of hip pain**

The policy states:

> "All other potential sources of hip pain have been ruled out."

[To be confirmed by Dr. Duval: the differential diagnoses considered and ruled out.] My records do also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

---

## A request about the criteria that were actually applied

Two of the excerpts above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I was not given in full. So that I can respond completely and fairly, I ask Aetna to identify in writing **which specific criteria of Aetna CPB 0736 – Hip Preservation Surgery the reviewer found unmet, and which documents the reviewer had in hand** when the 2026-08-19 decision was made.

I want to be clear about what this appeal does and does not claim. I am quoting only the policy language I have been able to obtain; I am not quoting any additional requirement, threshold, or section beyond the excerpts reproduced above, and where my records do not state a value, I have not supplied one.

The denial was based on incomplete documentation rather than on a finding that my hip does not need surgery. If the file was incomplete, I am asking for the opportunity to complete it. Dr. Duval and my physical therapist can provide the imaging report, the operative-planning and examination notes, and the physical therapy discharge note on request, and I authorize their release for this appeal.

---

## What I am asking Aetna to do

1. Overturn the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), reference POC-06FC809FB2-91216, and approve the procedure; or
2. If any criterion is still considered unmet, tell me in writing which one, and request the specific records named above from Dr. Duval and my physical therapist before issuing a final decision.
3. Provide me with a copy of the clinical review criteria used and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination.

I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals). My denial notice states that my appeal must be received **within 180 days of the date of the notice, by 2027-02-15**, and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending it by fax to **859-425-3379** and/or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I have confirmed before sending.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at this. I can be reached at [phone] or [email] if anything further is needed, and I would rather be asked for a document than have my request closed for lack of one.

Sincerely,

**Harper Grant**
Member ID: W271226534
Date of birth: [DOB]
Reference number: POC-06FC809FB2-91216

**Enclosures:**
- Aetna Member Complaint and Appeal Form
- Copy of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-19
- MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-07-17 [to be attached]
- Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-18 to 2026-07-25 [to be attached]
- Office and examination notes from Duval, MD [to be attached]
- Records of NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-10 [to be attached]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
